messages:
jamie: FYI I hit a weird rollback scenario after a tiny policy tweak this morning. traffic started drifting to lower-cost models for a subset of tenants. not a catastrophe but enough to trigger alerts. proposal: build a sim-driven preflight that replays sanitized traces against a policy delta before rollout. must cover cache states, region outages, cost spikes, and tenant budget envelopes.

sam: absolutely. deterministic replay is key. add a way to inject budget envelopes and request-rate ceilings so we can catch starvation and thrash. outputs should include switching-rate, latency deltas (median/p95), and cost delta per 1k requests.

maria: for cost signals we should accept a tiny DSL: piecewise linear, step, and gaussian noise. sim should accept a file like cost.yaml to model promos/spot spikes. also store immutable policy snapshots (id + metadata) so we can trace regressions later.

olivia: implementation sketch: a small library `policy-sim` that can import policy graphs (json), run the evaluator deterministically, and replay traces from a scrubbed trace store. CLI prototype: `rwd-policy-sim run --replay traces/2026-03-20.json --seed 42 --cache-warm 0.1 --inject-region us-east-1:0.2 --cost-signal cost.yaml --out sim-20260320.json`. produce a compact delta-report with per-tenant diffs and artifacts (heatmap, csv, culprit-samples).

jamie: good. need to explicitly exercise KV cache semantics — same policy can behave very differently if prefix cache is warmed. can sim accept kv-hit-profile (cold/steady/high-locality) and a `cache-warm` float?

sam: yes. add `--kv-hit-profile` with presets. also add `--fast-mode` that uses latency models instead of heavy kernels for quick CI checks; keep full-fidelity nightly runs that pull runtime decision logic.

maria: strong preference to reuse the runtime's decision code where possible. even if we don't run kernels, the adapter/kernel-selection logic should be identical to prod to avoid false negatives. maybe extract a thin evaluator module from runtime that is trivial to run in sim.

olivia: agreed. evaluator should be tiny and well-tested. for speed, fast-mode can stub latency but still run exact decision paths. full-fidelity mode runs parity checks against runtime component snapshots.

policy-sim-bot: sim-run-id=sim-20260320-42 | switching-rate=3.4% | median-latency=+12ms | p95-latency=+60ms | cost-per-1k=+$0.23 | issues: route-oscillation detected for tenant:alpha when budget<5% (repro-id=osc-771)

jamie: this output is ideal. we should surface stability heatmaps (time vs switching-rate) and top-n culprit request fingerprints that triggered flips. include reproducible re-run commands.

sam: sim artifacts: heatmap png, delta csv, culprit-samples.jsonl (n=20, redacted). include `rwd-policy-sim replay-culprits sim-20260320.jsonl --seed 42` so reviewers can re-run just the failure set.

maria: ops question: where do heavy sims run? my vote: nightly full-fidelity in a dedicated infra project, and fast pre-merge checks in CI with capped runtime. additionally, canary rollouts should be gated on sim thresholds (e.g., switching-rate<1% && p95<+10ms || cost delta < +$0.10/1k). thresholds configurable per-tenant.

olivia: I can add a rollout UI attachment that surfaces sim summary for each policy change. quick UX: green if thresholds pass, amber if borderline, red if exceed. also show top-5 impacted tenants and a link to artifacts.

jamie: owner for a prototype RFC + POC? I'll draft the RFC. need someone to pair on evaluator prototype.

sam: I can prototype the replay harness and evaluator this sprint. will mock cost DSL and kv profiles.

maria: I'll help with integration tests and define a parity checklist (decision points, kernel selection hooks, cache semantics, region penalties).

olivia: I'll wire the CLI and rollout UI attachment POC.

jamie: ok i'll include in RFC: sim architecture, artifacts, gating criteria, infra cost estimate, and an escalation playbook for failed sim gates. ping here with PR links. :thumbsup:

sam: filing a tracker ticket and dropping a tiny scrubbed trace + toy cost.yaml in this thread for the POC.

policy-sim-bot: reminder: scrub traces before upload. recommended: `rwd-scrub --level high`. remove user ids, emails, and any private prompt content.

jamie: noted. thanks all, starting RFC draft now.
